findings.evidence:
- Finished add-index args set globalness via `IsGlobal`: `pkg/ddl/index.go:1082` (`IsGlobal: indexInfo.Global`).
- But v1 finished-args encoder records `isGlobals` from deprecated `Global`: `pkg/meta/model/job_args.go:1522` (`isGlobals[i] = arg.Global`).
- Downstream delete-range logic relies on `IndexArg.IsGlobal`: `pkg/ddl/delete_range.go:363`.
- First-parent behavior stored globalness explicitly: `f1034dc3d42b5015ae2fcb015c1a6da4f36afee8:pkg/ddl/index.go:1118` (`isGlobal = append(isGlobal, indexInfo.Global)`).
findings.fix: In `pkg/meta/model/job_args.go` `(*ModifyIndexArgs).getFinishedArgsV1`, change `isGlobals[i] = arg.Global` to `isGlobals[i] = arg.IsGlobal` (and add a unit test with `IsGlobal=true`).
findings.impact: For JobVersion1 (current default), finished add-index jobs for global indexes will persist `isGlobal=false`, so `gc_delete_range` insertion treats global indexes as local (per-partition physical IDs). This can skip deleting temp/global-index key ranges (storage leak / incorrect GC range bookkeeping) and may cause prolonged space usage after add-index completion/cancel.
findings.verify:
- Unit: build a `Job{Version:JobVersion1, Type:ActionAddIndex}`; call `FillFinishedArgs(&ModifyIndexArgs{OpType:OpAddIndex, IndexArgs:[]*IndexArg{{IndexID:1, IsGlobal:true}}, PartitionIDs:[]int64{1}})`; encode/decode; `GetFinishedModifyIndexArgs` must return `IndexArgs[0].IsGlobal==true`.
- Behavior: add a global index on a partitioned table and inspect `mysql.gc_delete_range` entries; they should reference `tableID` (not partition IDs) for that index’s temp ranges.
findings.what: JobVersion1 finished add-index args lose the global-index flag: encoder uses `IndexArg.Global` instead of `IndexArg.IsGlobal`, so global indexes are treated as non-global in delete-range/GC paths.

findings.evidence:
- Unique-index BDR denial only inspects first index arg: `pkg/ddl/bdr.go:98` (`IndexArgs[0].Unique`).
- Multi-schema merge can produce a single add-index subjob with multiple `IndexArgs`: `pkg/ddl/multi_schema_change.go:358` (appends `args.IndexArgs...`).
findings.fix: In `pkg/ddl/bdr.go` `DeniedByBDR`, iterate over all `args.(*model.ModifyIndexArgs).IndexArgs` and deny if any `Unique` is true (and keep ActionAddPrimaryKey denied as well). Add a unit test with 2 IndexArgs where only the second is unique.
findings.impact: In BDR primary role, a multi-schema change that adds multiple indexes can bypass the “no unique index” restriction when the unique index is not the first element in the merged `ModifyIndexArgs`, potentially violating BDR safety/consistency expectations.
findings.verify: Add a unit test constructing `ModifyIndexArgs{IndexArgs:[{Unique:false},{Unique:true}]}` and assert `DeniedByBDR(BDRRolePrimary, ActionAddIndex, args)==true`.
findings.what: BDR unique-index restriction checks only `IndexArgs[0]`, so merged multi-index add-index jobs can slip through if a later index is unique.

subject: ddl: args v2 for add/drop/rename index, include PK/vector-index (#56130)
summary: Found 2 High correctness issues in this commit’s DDL args refactor: (1) JobVersion1 finished add-index args drop the global-index flag due to `arg.Global` vs `arg.IsGlobal` mismatch, breaking delete-range/GC behavior for global indexes; (2) BDR unique-index denial checks only the first index arg, so merged multi-index add-index jobs can bypass the restriction. Neither is fixed in `remotes/upstream/master@f0813a3696`.
